Block ports and signals

Source: vignettes/ports-and-signals.Rmd
ports-and-signals.Rmd
library(simcompR)

Every block declares its input and output ports explicitly. This vignette explains how ports are numbered and named, how signal sizes are determined and which connections are rejected.

Ports, numbers and names

Ports are numbered from 1. Most blocks have one output; some have several (for example demux, or state_machine). Ports also have names, which can be used instead of numbers once the block’s parameters are known.

m <- sim_model("ports")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "v", value = c(1, 2, 3))
sim_add_block(m, "demux", "split", sizes = c(1, 2))
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "double", gain = 2)
sim_connect(m, "v", "split")
sim_connect(m, "split", "double", output = "out2")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 1), times = 1)
sim_signal(r, c("split.out1", "split.out2", "double"))
#>    split.out1 split.out2[1] split.out2[2]     double[1]     double[2] 
#>             1             2             3             4             6

Signals are named after the block that produces them. A block with one output port is named by the block name ("double"); otherwise the port name is appended ("split.out2"). Vector signals have one column per element.

The block library

sim_block_types() lists every registered type, its category and its parameters.

types <- sim_block_types()
table(types$category)
#> 
#> continuous   discrete      logic       math    routing       sink     source 
#>          4          5          5         13          3          3         10 
#>  subsystem 
#>          3
types[types$category == "math", c("type", "parameters")]
#>          type        parameters
#> 1         abs                  
#> 4   dead_zone      lower, upper
#> 9      divide                  
#> 10 expression        expr, size
#> 11        fcn         fun, size
#> 13       gain              gain
#> 17     lookup x, y, extrapolate
#> 18       math               fun
#> 19     minmax     fun, n_inputs
#> 24    product               ops
#> 28 saturation      lower, upper
#> 38   subtract                  
#> 39        sum             signs

Signal types

All signals are real numeric vectors of a fixed size. Logical values are carried as numbers: 1 for true and 0 for false, and logic blocks treat any nonzero input as true. There is no silent conversion of R logical vectors or matrices at ports: a block that produces the wrong length is an error.

Signal sizes

Sizes are either fixed by a block (a constant with three values has an output of size 3, an integrator has the size of its initial state) or inherited (a scalar gain has the size of its input). Compilation propagates sizes along connections until every port has a size:

m <- sim_model("sizes")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "r", value = c(1, -1))
sim_add_block(m, "sum", "e", signs = "+-")
sim_add_block(m, "integrator", "x", initial = c(0, 0))
sim_connect(m, "r", "e", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "x", "e", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "e", "x")
plan <- sim_compile(m)
plan$sizes$out
#> $e
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $r
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $x
#> [1] 2

Scalar expansion, and nothing else

Elementwise blocks (sum, product, minmax, logic, switch) accept inputs of equal size or scalars. A scalar input is expanded to the common size. This is the only implicit size rule. R’s usual recycling of a length 2 vector against a length 3 vector is refused:

m <- sim_model("recycling")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "a", value = c(1, 2))
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "b", value = c(1, 2, 3))
sim_add_block(m, "sum", "s")
sim_connect(m, "a", "s", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "b", "s", input = 2)
sim_compile(m)
#> Error:
#> ! Block 's' (sum): input sizes 2, 3 are incompatible; inputs must have equal sizes or be scalars.

A fixed-size input fed by a signal of another size is also refused:

m <- sim_model("mismatch")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "a", value = c(1, 2))
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "K", gain = matrix(1, 2, 3))
sim_connect(m, "a", "K")
sim_compile(m)
#> Error:
#> ! Signal size mismatch: 'a' output 1 has size 2 but input 'in1' of block 'K' expects size 3.

Connection rules

The compiler rejects:

  • inputs that are not connected;
  • an input with more than one source;
  • ports or blocks that do not exist;
  • incompatible sizes.
m <- sim_model("open")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "a")
sim_add_block(m, "product", "p")
sim_connect(m, "a", "p", input = 1)
sim_compile(m)
#> Error:
#> ! Unconnected input port(s): p:in2.

An output may feed any number of inputs, and an output that feeds nothing is fine (its value is still recorded).

Routing blocks

mux concatenates inputs, demux splits a vector, and selector picks elements by index:

m <- sim_model("routing")
sim_add_block(m, "time", "t")
sim_add_block(m, "sine", "s")
sim_add_block(m, "mux", "both", n_inputs = 2)
sim_add_block(m, "selector", "second", index = 2)
sim_connect(m, "t", "both", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "s", "both", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "both", "second")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 1), times = c(0, 0.5, 1))
cbind(sim_signal(r, "both"), second = sim_signal(r, "second"))
#>      both[1]   both[2]    second
#> [1,]     0.0 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [2,]     0.5 0.4794255 0.4794255
#> [3,]     1.0 0.8414710 0.8414710

Recording with scopes

Every block output is recorded. A scope block marks a signal of interest: its input is available under the scope’s name and plot() shows scopes by default.

sim_add_block(m, "scope", "view")
sim_connect(m, "second", "view")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 6))
plot(r)

Units

Signals carry no units in this release. Keep units consistent within a model; unit checking is on the roadmap.
